notes: Independent reader r3, confined to cote 29 scan 113. Start time was captured from the UTC clock before any image view. Whole image, upper half and lower half were each displayed once; thirteen genuinely open places received one saved enlarged crop each. No display failed, no crop was repeated, and no half was reopened.

Every agreed word, sign and ending was checked against the appropriate half, including the field notation, powers and lower indices, closures, inequalities, inverse images, tensor products, both homomorphism targets, accents, terminal punctuation and the unfinished last line. Source drafts were not treated as authority.

The page states a Bertini geometric irreducibility assertion for a generic codimension-s linear section with s≤dim closure f(X)−1, then a local assertion using the bad locus Z and dim closure f(Z)<s. Corollary 3 claims fundamental-group surjectivity under conditions 1 and non-respective 2 with an inserted algebraically closed-field assumption. The remark states properness and prime-to-characteristic-quotient variants. These are document claims, not theorems verified in this run.

Written reservation transcribed exactly: On n’affirme pas, cependant, que (*) soit toujours surjectif (sans hypothèse de propreté sur X). It withholds an unrestricted assertion; it is not a statement that the preceding proper case is unproved.

The mathematical content only located optical questions: the ≤/</subset signs, closure bars, π indices, source letter in (**), and exclamation superscripts. No mathematical expectation was used to change X/Y, supply a symbol, choose the numeral history, or repair the spelling èd/xposant.

Title: Théorème de Bertini et variantes. This is a text page, not a separate title sheet. No own page number, date, or stated total page count is present. Pencil archive number 112 is transcribed as a comment. Numbered headings are theorem 1, local statement 2, corollary 3, an overprinted remark number 3/4, and the beginning of corollary 4.

There are three displayed homomorphisms, two written display labels at the left, five marginal nonverbal strokes/braces, two handwritten marginal notes, and no mathematical diagram. The last Corollary 4 sentence is unfinished at the page boundary; nothing is supplied beyond si X.

The cancelled heading and two local handwritten soits are distinct: the live first soit is before f; the earlier cancelled soit is between est and ramifié. The inserted Supposons k alg. clos. is anchored before Alors, after non respé.

H’s subsection/bold/emphasis macros are treated as heading or emphasis encodings, not literal bold type. Their macro names alone are not differences. Missing handwritten wrappers alone are not differences. The inserted state and the independently missing accent in Énoncé are material differences. The archive number is not counted as an H omission because of extraction conventions.

The supplied C_prior_questions.md initially contained two unrelated scan-116 bullets despite its stated page-only scope. They were disregarded. A later administrative message confirmed their accidental inclusion; no other page was opened and no scan-113 reading was changed because of it.

Handwriting is inventoried as an unnamed hand; no authorship attribution is made from the image. The use of that inventory category does not establish a second historical person. Some tiny overprint sequences remain without an assigned correction chronology.

No OCR, text recognition, PDF text extraction, research, other-page inspection, other-reader inspection, or extra agent was used. No targeted proof check, independent re-proof, computation or formal certificate was performed; the checks array is deliberately empty.
